items.title: Reduce the signed Gaussian formula to the norm axis

source.anchor: AppendixB2 standing range; AppendixB2.2 Ex58 and following p4.2 axis quadratic form e1^T A_O e1=(kappa+1-(kappa-1)U)/2. Literal Gaussian-formula average only.
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS makes the orthogonal-transitivity and coordinate adapter explicit; actual Gaussian-law identification is separate.

items.statement: Let n>=3 and kappa>=4, let O have the existing normalized Borel Haar probability on full real O(n), and let A_O be the exact equation4 precision. Define the literal function p_O(v)=sqrt(det A_O)/(2pi)^(n/2) exp(-v^T A_O v/2), with a real dimension-half exponent. For every x in Euclidean real n-space, put U=O_11 and r_O(x)=sqrt(det A_O)/(2pi)^(n/2) exp(-(kappa+1-(kappa-1)U)||x||_2^2/4). Both O -> det(O)p_O(x) and O -> det(O)r_O(x) are absolutely integrable under that Haar probability, and their expectations are equal. All vectors, including zero and vectors already on the norm axis, are included. The claim is for these explicit functions; it does not identify p with a Gaussian probability density.
assumptions: AppendixB2 standing n>=3 and kappa>=4 are retained. Every x belongs to the actual EuclideanSpace R (Fin n); its norm is the Euclidean norm, never the coordinate sup norm.
The law is the same actual canonical normalized full-O(n) Borel Haar probability, allowing reflections and both determinant signs. The matrix A_O is the unchanged literal source precision.
WithLp.ofLp converts a Euclidean vector to its real coordinates for dotProduct and mulVec. Source coordinate1 is the zero-based j0, whose validity follows from n>=3.

Both Haar L1 assertions are outputs. No orthogonal witness, equal-norm premise, covariance identity, integrability assumption, Gaussian density identification or spatial Fubini assumption is supplied by the caller. All dimension-half powers are real.

formulae.label: Literal norm-axis reduction and O11 exponent

obligations.label: Genuine-L1 literal signed Haar norm-axis equality and exact first-entry Gaussian exponent

bindings.boundary: The literal-function Ex58 norm-axis average and its following O11 exponent are proved, including both fixed-vector Haar L1 outputs. Actual N(0,A_O^-1) law/density identification, probability normalization/covariance, joint spatial/Haar domination and Fubini, original H(lambda) identification, Ex59 sharp domination, sphere/Poisson, TV/amplification/transcript/eigenbasis and both main lower bounds remain open. No Gaussian probability measure is defined by the local formulas.

assumption_deltas.source: Standing n>=3,kappa>=4; full Haar O(n), every Euclidean x. Ex58 uses orthogonal transitivity and p4.2 evaluates the axis quadratic form.
assumption_deltas.lean: Same standing range, law, precision and Euclidean norm. Reflection and actual orthogonal coordinate witness, both Haar L1 conclusions and exact axis exponent are produced internally. Formula-to-Gaussian-law identification remains excluded.
assumption_deltas.reason: The binding covers the literal-function norm-axis calculation only. Uniform reflection handles zero/equal vectors without a new premise or off-source fallback. No actual Gaussian-law, spatial Fubini or main-bound claim is added.
